name: Bulgogi KBBQ Meal Prep
blurb: Who doesn't love Korean BBQ? I got this recipe idea from one of my clients. They loved eating all- you-can-eat Korean BBQ on Friday nights out, but struggled with knowing how many calories they were consuming since it's nearly impossible to track. And this recipe is meant to solve this very specific but VERY real problem. Paired with my healthier version of that iconic, spicy Korean house salad you get at Korean BBQ, this meal is meant to bring all the flavors we know and love, but more macro friendly!
ingredients: labeled as Bulgogi meat at your
steps: Slice your yellow onion and green onions into thin strips. Slice your Persian cucumbers into thin strips. Chop your green leaf lettuce into small pieces.

In a bowl, combine your honey, minced garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and black pepper to make your marinade. In a large bowl, add in your sliced meat and sliced yellow onions and pour your marinade on top.
Mix everything well. Marinate for 30min-5 hours in the fridge for the best flavor.
On a pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, grill your bulgogi mix until cooked through.

In a new bowl, to make your salad, combine your minced garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, gochugaru, sesame oil, sesame seeds, cucumber slices, chopped lettuce, and sliced green onions and mix well.
In a meal prep container, add half your steamed rice, half your bulgogi, and half your salad. Repeat for your second meal prep container.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to reheat, make sure to put your salad and meat into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed, then add in your meat and microwave till warm. Finally, finally add in your veggies on top to preserve the crunch and enjoy!

name: Spicy BBQ Gochujang Chicken Meal Prep
blurb: Gochujang is a spicy Korean paste that's slightly sweet with a kick. So using this iconic Korean
ingredients: ingredient and turning it into a glaze is the perfect
way to add way more flavor if you find your usual
chicken and rice meal preps boring.
I like to pair this with edamame and cucumbers for
8 oz boneless skinless chicken thighs raw
2 tbsp soy sauce (1 tbsp for marinade and 1 tbsp for glaze)
steps: Slice your cucumbers into circles, dice your green onions, and peel your edamame In a bowl, combine honey, brown sugar, rice vinegar, salt, 1 tbsp soy sauce, gochujang, and sesame oil to make your glaze.

In a new bowl, add in your chicken thighs, 1 tbsp soy sauce, minced garlic, and minced ginger and rub the marinade into the chicken thighs. Marinate for 30min-5 hours in the fridge for the best flavor.
On a piece of parchment paper, lay your marinaded chicken thighs flat. Then, brush the gochujang glaze to fully coat all of the chicken thighs.
Place the chicken thighs on the parchment paper into your airfrier at 370 Fahrenheit for 17-20min (cooking time will very depending on your airfrier). Cook until golden brown and cooked through.
In a meal prep container, add half your steamed rice, half your chicken topped with sesame seeds, and half your edamame and cucmbers. Repeat for your second meal prep container.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to re-heat, make sure to put your salad & meat into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed, then add in your meat and microwave till warm, and finally add in your veggies on top to preserve the crunch and enjoy!

name: Honey Sriracha Shrimp Meal Prep
blurb: This recipe is perfect if you're new to cooking. It's super simple and easy to make for the amount of flavor you get in return. Shrimp has one of the best calorie to protein ratios out there, but it can be a little boring on it's own. So cooking it in a spicy, sweet, and savory sauce, I always find myself coming back to this recipe on my busier weeks.
ingredients: 1 lb Argentine red shrimp raw frozen, thawed
steps: Dice your green onions, slice your cucumber, and peel your edamame Thaw your frozen raw shrimp, pat dry, and season with red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper On a pan coated with spray oil on medium-low heat, cook your shrimp until it turns to a light orange/pink color (fully cooked). Remove the cooked shrimp and set aside In a bowl, mix your soy sauce, honey, siracha, and olive oil to make your sauce.
In a new pan on low heat, pour this sauce mixture into the pan.

Immediately follow by pouring in your cornstarch slurry, which is a mixture of 1 tsp cornstarch and 2 tsp water in a small bowl. Mix the cornstarch slurry into the sauce to let it thicken a little to turn into a glaze, then immediately remove from the heat.
In a bowl, add your cooked shrimp, pour your slightly thickened sauce, and mix well.
In a meal prep container, add your cooked rice, shrimp, edamame, diced green onions, and cucumber slices and enjoy!

This full recipe is intended to be split into 4 even meal prep containers, but for larger portions, you can also choose to split it into 2 even meals (you'd just have to double the macros/calories since you'd be eating double the intended serving size)!

name: Chicken Katsu Meal Prep
blurb: Katsu is one of my favorite ways to enjoy chicken. There's a local Katsu shop near where I live and it's one of my favorite guilty pleasures since it's not a low calorie food. But when I found you can make the same crunch with panko breadcrumbs and juciness using an airfrier, this recipe became something I'd make for my girlfriend and family over and over again. Dipped in my take on a lower calorie katsu sauce, this recipe easily makes my top 5 list of all time for delicious meal preps.
ingredients: 16oz raw chicken thighs (seasoned with salt & pepper)
steps: Lightly season your chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Pound your seasoned chicken thighs to half an inch thick.
Crack and whisk the eggs, flour, water, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, and 1 tsp garlic powder to make a batter-like consistency.

Pour panko breadcrumbs on a plate. Fully dip the chicken thighs into the batter, place it on top of the panko breadcrumbs and mix until fully coated, and put it into the air frier. Repeat this dipping into the batter and coating with panko breadcrumb process with every chicken thigh.
Coat the top of the chicken with a quick spray of oil.
Cook for 360°F for 10 min then flip & cook for another 7-10 minutes until the inside is completely cooked through & the crust is crispy brown (cooking times vary with different airfriers).
Mix ketchup, brown sugar, worcestershire sauce, 3/4 tbsp garlic, and oyster sauce to make your katsu sauce.
In a meal prep container, add a third of your steamed rice, a third of your katsu, and a third of your sauce on the side. Repeat for your other 2 meal prep containers.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to re-heat, make sure to put your sauce in a small separate container & chicken into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed, then add in your meat and microwave till warm. Finally, finally top it off with your sauce and enjoy!

name: Sesame Salmon Meal Prep
blurb: My clients LOVE this one. It's easy to make in a batch, requires little cooking experience, and tasty even when reheated. This meal prep not only is packed with protein, but also provides you a ton of Omega-3 fatty acids which is a win-win.
steps: Grab your salmon and rub it with a mix of salt, lemon pepper, 1 tsp garlic powder, and paprika.
In a bowl, mix together garlic powder, soy sauce, sesame oil, sriracha, lemon juice, and rice wine vinegar to create your sauce.
Slice your salmon into 1 inch by 1 inch cubes.
Pour half of the sauce on your salmon cubes.
Place the salmon cubes on a tray lined with parchment paper and put in the oven to cook at 415°F 10-12 mins, flipping it halfway through (or until crispy and cooked through).
Lay the salmon over a bed of steamed white rice, steamed edamame, and sliced cucumbers. Pour the rest of your sauce on top and enjoy.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to re-heat, make sure to put your sauce in a small separate container and place your veggies and salmon into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed, then add in your salmon and microwave till warm. Finally, finally top it off with your veggies and sauce and enjoy!

name: Kung Pao Chicken Meal Prep
blurb: If I had to name only 3 fast food restaurants to eat for the rest of my life, one would definitely be Panda Express. One of my favorite things to get there is their Orange Chicken and Kung Pao chicken. So, this is my take on Kung Pao Chicken with a slightly healthier spin and is one of my recipes that my mom raves about.
ingredients: 3-5 dried red chili peppers or Chile de arbol (arbol chilies)
steps: Dice your red, yellow and green bell peppers into small pieces and thinly slice your onion.
On a pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, add in your diced veggies and minced garlic and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
To make the Kung Pao sauce, in a bowl, combine your soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and hoisin sauce and mix.
Slice your chicken thighs seasoned with salt and pepper into small cubes and add them into the pan with the veggies and sauté until chicken is cooked through.
Add your dried red chili peppers and peanuts into the pan and continue to sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Make a cornstarch slurry by mixing together cornstarch and water in a small bowl.
Pour in your sauce into the pan and immediately add in your cornstarch slurry.
Continue to stir for 1-2 minutes on medium heat to slightly thicken the sauce and incorporate it into the chicken and veggies, then remove from the heat.
In a meal prep container, add a third of your steamed rice and a third of your Kung Pao chicken and top it off with sliced green onions. Repeat for your other 2 meal prep containers.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to re-heat, make sure to put your chicken into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed and then add in your chicken and microwave till warm and enjoy!

name: Orange Chicken Meal Prep
blurb: Well, I said I loved Panda Express earlier, and their orange chicken is my other go-to item! So this is my healthier take on the classic recipe. It's my guilt-free way of enjoying one of my favorite take out items more often!
steps: In a bowl, add in orange juice, chicken broth, soy sauce, brown sugar, sriracha, rice vinegar, white pepper, cornstarch and set aside.
Get your chicken, chop it into small cubes, season with salt, sesame oil, and cornstarch.
In a pan on medium heat coated with spray oil, cook your cubed chicken. Mix in minced garlic and orange zest and cook till chicken is golden brown.
Once chicken is cooked through, add in your sauce and stir on low heat until the sauce starts to slightly thicken, then remove from the heat.

In a meal prep container, add a your cooked rice, some steamed broccoli (microwave broccoli in a bowl covered with a wet paper towel for a quick steam), and your orange chicken topped with diced green onions and sesame seeds.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to re-heat, make sure to put your chicken and brocolli into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed and then add in your chicken and microwave till warm and add in your broccoli and enjoy!

name: Kimchi Shrimp Fried Rice Meal Prep
blurb: This recipe is, funnily enough, something that got me through college. There's nothing better than using some leftover kimchi, a few simple
ingredients: ingredients, and frozen shrimp and just throwing it
all together for a filling, macro-friendly meal.
"College Meals" have a bad stigma for not tasting
good, but this is the one exception, hence why I
2-3 tbsp kimchi juice (depending on desired saltiness level)
3 sheets of roasted salted seaweed snack (shredded)
steps: Dice your green into small pieces and thinly slice your white onions.

Coat a pan with spray oil, leave it on medium-low heat, and add in your kimchi and rice and mix Push your kimchi-rice mixture to one side of the pan, and on the other side of the pan, add your shrimp and season with leftover kimchi juice, salt, pepper, and onion powder.
Pour in your egg whites on the same side as your shrimp and add in your white onions.
Once the shrimp & egg whites are cooked, quickly mix it all together and stiry fry.
Transfer your fried rice to your meal prep container and top it off with your diced green onions and sesame seeds.
Reheat in a microwave by covering your meal prep container with a wet paper towel and enjoy!

name: Chicken Bulgogi Ssam Meal Prep
blurb: Ssam is a Korean technique where you wrap your meal in a bed of lettuce leaves like a wrap. There's no better way to enjoy it than with Bulgogi. So, to save on some calories, I like using chicken thighs cooked in that classic bulgogi marinade we all know and love.
steps: Cut your chicken into strips place it into a bowl.
Thinly slice your white onions, dice your green onions, and then add them into the bowl.
Add into the same bowl your soy sauce, mirin or sake, brown sugar, minced garlic, sesame oil, and black pepper and mix well. Let it marinate for 15 minutes to a few hours in the fridge.
On a pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, add in your bowl of chicken & veggies.
Cook until chicken has a slight crisp and is cooked through.
In a meal prep container, add 1⁄3 of your cooked rice, some lettuce leaves, and 1⁄3 of your chicken topped with sesame seeds. Repeat 2 more times.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to reheat, make sure to put your chicken and lettuce into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed and then add in your chicken and microwave till warm. Grab your lettuce leaf, add some rice and chicken on top, wrap it up as a "Ssam" (aka wrap), and enjoy!

name: Vietnamese Shaken Beef (Bo Luc Lac) Meal Prep
blurb: I tried Bo Luc Lac for the first time when my Vietnamese girlfriend's family invited me over for dinner and made this savory, slightly sweet, and peppery dish. After my frist bite, this meal instantly became my favorite Vietnamese dish right next to pho. So, I spent the next few weeks trying to turn it into a meal prep so I can enjoy it more often and I can't wait for you to try it too!
steps: Dice your tomato and cucumbers into small cubes, dice your lettuce into small pieces, and thinly slice your onion.
Slice your beef into 1 inch cubes.
In a bowl, add in your beef cubes and oyster sauce, soy sauce, salt, ground black pepper, cornstarch, baking soda, and minced garlic and mix well.
On a pan on medium heat coated with spray oil, grill your meat until almost cooked through then add your sliced red onions and sauté.

In your meal prep container, add 1/2 of your steamed rice topped with 1/2 of your shaken beef. On the side, add 1/2 of your salad of tomato and cucumber slices with chopped lettuce. Top the salad and beef off with additional ground black pepper and salt to taste. When ready to eat, mix it all together and enjoy.

Pro tip: when meal prepping to reheat, make sure to put your salad & meat into separate ziploc bags to avoid getting the rice soggy. When ready to eat, microwave the rice with a wet paper towel first to get it steamed, then add in your meat and microwave till warm.
Finally, add in your veggies on top preserve the crunch!

name: Bulgogi Gimbap Wrap
blurb: When you think of Korean food, one of the foods that tend to come to mind is gimbap. But the average gimbap can pack a surprisingly large amount of calories from the rice and sesame oil. So for this recipe, I turned gimbap into a delicious Bulgogi "sushi wrap" with some Nori sheets, kimchi, a fried egg, and some steamed rice. It's a creative way to enjoy everyone's favorite Korean roll.
ingredients: 3oz thinly sliced ribeye raw (also labeled as Bulgogi meat at your local Korean
1 full sheet nori (sheet of roasted seaweed)
steps: In a bowl, mix together sesame oil, minced garlic, soy sauce, honey, sesame seeds, and black pepper to make your marinade.
Add into the marinade your sliced meat and mix well.
On a pan coated with spray oil on medium-low heat, cook your marinated meat until cooked through, then remove.
On the same pan, crack and cook a sunny side up egg.
Grab a square sheet of nori and cut a slit halfway up into the nori and lightly crease/fold the nori to visualize 4 equal square shaped quadrants.

In each of the 4 quadrants of the nori, add half your cooked rice on the first quadrant, your cooked meat on the second quadrant, your cooked egg topped with kimchi on the third quadrant, and the rest of your rice on the fourth quadrant.
Fold each quadrant on top of each other until you create one thick square wrap. Cut in half and enjoy!

name: Shrimp Rice Paper Noodles
blurb: A tasty noodle dish is something I missed so much during my weight loss journey. Unfortunately, most noodle recipes out there just pack a ton of calories from the noodles alone. I wish I found this recipe years ago because it's a great way to get the same flavor and texture for a fraction of the calories!
ingredients: 3 oz large shrimp raw (argentine red shrimp)
steps: Dice your green onions into small pieces.
In a large plate, pour a thin layer of drinking water and dip both sides of your rice paper into the water to make it moist.
Transport and lay the wet rice paper flat onto another plate, repeat, and stack the rest of your wet rice paper sheets on top of each other.

Pour some drinking water over the stack of wet rice paper so it stays hydrated. This makes it easier to slice since it doesn't dry up and thus won't get sticky. Cut the stack of wet rice papers into 1/2 inch thick strips.
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, brown sugar, 1-2 tsp water (depending on your preference), and minced garlic and mix.
In a pan coated with spray oil, grill your raw shrimp.
Plate by adding the noodles into a bowl and your grilled shrimp on top. Then sprinkle with sesame seeds and your diced green onions, and pour the sauce on top and enjoy!

name: Tunacado Sandwich
blurb: I know, I know...this isn't an "Asian-inspired" recipe. What the heck Joe! I said this was a MOSTLY Asian-inspired recipe cookbook. Sometimes I just like a good sandwich and this is a simple recipe I just love because of how easy it is to make and requires zero cooking.
ingredients: 4 slices of "Thin-Sliced 21 whole grains and seeds" Dave's Killer Bread
steps: Dice your red onions into small pieces and cut two large tomato slices In a bowl add in your drained canned tuna, avocado, light mayo, Greek yogurt, diced red onions, dill, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, and Salt and pepper to taste and mix well.
Toast 4 slices of bread and add one tomato slice, half the tuna mix, and half the pesto per sandwich and make two sandwiches and enjoy!

name: Microwave Hot Pot
blurb: My girlfriend and I love going out for a hot pot dinner date. Nothing beats that warm, savory broth with all those toppings. But obviously, it's impossible to know how many calories are in what we're eating. So, this recipe bring your favorite hot pot flavors home without needing anything but a microwave to do all the cooking. If you love simple, tasty, lazy meals...this one's for you! Carbohydrates: 33g
ingredients: 3oz thinly sliced ribeye (labeled "hot pot beef" at your local Asian market)
steps: Dice your green onion into small pieces and slice your tofu into thin rectangles.

In a microwave safe bowl, add your beansprout, korean rice cakes, sliced tofu, enoki mushrooms, beef brisket slices, beef bone broth, minced garlic, water, soy sauce, honey, black and pepper and salt.
Cover everything with 3 large leaves of napa cabbage.
Cover the bowl with a paper plate and microwave it for 6 minutes or until fully cooked.
Make your dipping sauce by combining soy sauce and wasabi.
Cut everything with scissors into bite sized pieces and enjoy!

name: Korean-Inspired Omelette
blurb: Omelettes are one of the best ways to start your morning. This omelette recipe is a spin on the classic recipe but with Korean flavors. Adding rice and kimchi on the side is optional, but in my opinion, two must haves.
ingredients: 5oz thinly sliced beef brisket (commonly found at your local Korean market)
optional: pair with rice and kimchi (not accounted for in the macros/calories)
steps: Dice your green onion into small pieces and thinly slice your yellow onion.
To make your marinade, combine soy sauce, brown sugar, gochugaru, and beef bone broth.
On a non-stick pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, add your thinly sliced beef brisket and heat till cooked.
Lower the heat to medium-low, add your sliced yellow onions, and pour your marinade in the pan and sauté.
Crack and whisk together two eggs in a bowl and pour it over everything in the pan and fill all the gaps to make one circular omelette.
Season with salt and black pepper and add your diced green onions on top.
This is optional, but I like to lay it over steamed rice and pair it with kimchi and enjoy!

name: Beef Pepper Rice
blurb: If you've ever tried the sizzling beef pepper rice, you know it's delicious. This concept is inspired from the viral Pepper Lunch restaurant. The goal with this recipe was to bring you all of the same flavors, but a little healthier so you can enjoy it more often.
steps: Dice your yellow onions into long, thin strips and dice your green onions into small pieces.
On a pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, cook your top sirloin topped with salt and pepper until desired doneness.
Move the meat to one side of the pan add in your diced onions and frozen corn into the pan.
In a separate small bowl, combine together your sesame seeds, honey, soy sauce, and garlic powder and mix well to make your sauce.
Cook a sunny side up egg.
Add your cooked rice onto the original pan, place the sunny side up egg on top, an add your butter on the steak.
Top it off with your diced green onions and pour the sauce you made on top.
Mix it together in the pan like a fried rice or eat it separately and enjoy!

name: Spicy Tofu Bowl
blurb: I used to hate tofu growing up, but realized I just never knew the right way to enjoy it. This tofu with it's spicy sauce is something my Koream mom made for me time and time again growing up. But to make it a more filling meal, I like turning it into a salad with rice and veggies.
ingredients: 13.5 oz of soft tofu/silken tofu (usually one full block of tofu)
steps: Dice your jalapeno and 1 green onion into small pieces.
In a bowl, mix together soy sauce, sesame oil, brown sugar, gochugaru, sesame seeds, garlic powder, diced jalapeno, and 1 diced green onion and set aside.
Chop your lettuce into small pieces and thinly slice 1 green onion and set aside.
Take your soft tofu, drain the liquid, pat it dry, and create a grid of small slits with a knife while making sure not to cut all the way through the tofu.
Cover your tofu with a paper towel, place it in a bowl, and microwave it for 3 minutes.
Place your cooked rice in a bowl, lay your chopped lettuce and thinly sliced green onions on top, place your sliced block of cooked tofu on top of the veggies, and pour the sauce over the tofu.

name: Salmon Sushi Bake
blurb: If my girlfriend had to pick one of her favorite recipes from this cookbook, one would easily be this sushi bake. She saw this idea on her Instagram For You page many times and I recreated it to her liking. Who would've thought such a creative dish was also so macro-friendly? Ingredients (makes 2 servings):
ingredients: Optional: salted roasted seaweed (not included in the macros/calories)
steps: Season your salmon with salt, pepper, paprika, and garlic powder. Make sure to get an even coat.
Lay your salmon on parchment paper and bake in the oven at 400F for 12 minutes until cooked through.
Get your cooked rice and put that and the cooked salmon in a large bowl. Drizzle the siracha, kewpie mayo, and soy sauce on top. Mix it all together with a fork.
Place it in an empty tray, sprinkle with sesame seeds, diced green onion, and furikake, and enjoy! This is optional, but it's best enjoyed with salted roasted seaweed.

name: Fresh Shrimp Spring Rolls
blurb: I've said this before and I'll say it again. Fresh spring rolls are one of THE best weight loss foods out there. It's so low calorie, easy to customize, quick to make, and you can pack it with tons of protein. I found shrimp to be the best to use since it's very lean. The sauce is from my Vietnamese girlfriend's mom's classic recipe and it pairs perfect with these fresh spring rolls.
steps: Cut your Persian cucumbers into long strips, tear your romaine lettuce into thin pieces, and dice your red chili pepper into small pieces.
On a pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, cook your raw shrimp.
Pour water onto a large plate and dip all sides of your sheet of rice paper into the water. Shake off any excess water.
On the wet sheet of rice paper, lay your strips of cucumber, romaine lettuce, and cooked shrimp and roll it like a burrito into a spring roll.
To make the sauce, mix your fish sauce, diced red chili pepper, minced garlic, brown sugar, and lemon juice in a small bowl.
Dip the spring rolls into your sauce and enjoy.

name: Lox Cucumber Salad
blurb: Lox bagels are my all time favorite brunch meal, but they aren't the most macro-friendly recipe due to the bagel adding so many calories. So instead, this recipe is the perfect alternative. Using cucumbers peeled like noodles, this salad is a delicious and unique way to enjoy lox. If you love lox like me, this recipe is for you.
ingredients: 3 tbsp 1/3 less fat cream cheese (Philadelphia brand)
steps: Peel your english cucumbers into long strips using a fruit or vegetable peeler and thinly slice your onions.
In a bowl, combine greek yogurt, cream cheese, white onion diced, capers, sesame seeds, lemon juice, minced garlic, dill, and salt and pepper to taste and mix.
Plate by adding in your peeled cucumbers and topping it off with smoked salmon and your sauce and enjoy!

name: Dakjuk (Korean Chicken And Rice Porridge)
blurb: Porridge, when made right, is not only for when you're feeling under the weather. Dakjuk is a flavorful and savory way to level up your boring porridge. Plus, it's a protein-packed meal filled with nutrients to keep you full for longer!
ingredients: 3/4 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thigh raw
steps: Dice your onions, green onions, and carrots into small pieces and mince your garlic.
In a blender, pour in your chicken bone broth and cooked rice and blend for 5-10 seconds.
In a pot on medium heat coated with spray oil, add your sesame oil, diced onions, minced garlic, and diced carrots and sauté.
Pour your blended rice into the pot and keep the heat on medium to bring it to a light boil.
Add in your diced raw chicken thighs to the pot and boil until the chicken is fully cooked through but make sure to keep stirring to avoid the rice from burning or sticking to the bottom.
Remove the chicken from the pot once cooked and use a fork to shred it into thin pieces.

Add the cooked, shredded chicken back into the pot, season the porridge with salt and pepper to taste, and top it off with your diced green onions, sesame seeds, and soy sauce and enjoy it with some fresh kimchi!

name: Chicken Yaki Udon
blurb: If I had a recipe that if I made for you, you would have no clue it was healthy, low calorie, and high protein, it would be this. Yaki udon is delicious, but oftentimes, is packed with a ton of calories due to the amount of oil and sauces used. So instead, I like to use chicken thighs and reduced ratios of oil and sauces to have better macros without compromising on taste.
steps: Dice your chicken into small cubes.
In a bowl, add your diced chicken and 1 tbsp soy sauce and mix well to marinate.
Make your sauce by mixing together oyster sauce, 2 tbsp soy sauce, mirin, black pepper, and water.
In a pot of boiling water, boil your fresh udon noodles until cooked. Once the noodles are cooked, add them into a bowl of ice cold water.
Add your marinated chicken cubes into a pan on medium heat coated with spray oil and cook until chicken is cooked through.
Add your sauce, diced napa cabbage, diced onions, diced mushrooms, and your cooked udon into the pan and stir fry.
Top it off with diced green onions and enjoy!

name: Rice Paper Shrimp Roll
blurb: If you like Dim Sum, you'll love this recipe. Most Dim Sum dishes are carb heavy, so instead when making it at home, I save on time and calories by using rice paper. I've had a few followers and clients of mine let me know this recipe made them feel like they were enjoying some Dim Sum, but at home and guilt- free.
ingredients: 4 oz argentine red shrimp frozen raw, thawed
steps: Dice your green onions and thawed shrimp into small pieces & pat dry your diced shrimp.
In a bowl, add salt, white pepper, cornstarch, sesame oil, and your diced shrimp and mix well.
Pour your water onto a large plate, wet your rice paper, shake off any excess water from the wet rice paper, and transfer to a dry plate.
Lay your shrimp mix in a line onto the wet rice paper and top it off with your diced green onions.
Roll your rice paper with the shrimp filling inside to create long rolls and repeat.
Place your rolls on a plate, coat it with spray oil, and place the plate in your steamer and steam for 8 minutes.
In a bowl, mix together soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, and water to make your sauce.
Once your shrimp rolls are ready, pour your sauce over the rolls and dip some chili oil on top and enjoy!

name: Tuna Salad Lettuce Wrap
blurb: Lettuce wraps are such an underrated way to enjoy some of your favorite sandwiches without the surplus of calories. Whenever I want something lighter and more fresh, tuna salad sandwiches are my go to. So this wrap variation is something I like to add to my rotation since it's a higher protein alternative.
steps: Dice your cucumbers and red onions and slice your avocados.
In a bowl, add your drained canned tuna, diced red onions, light mayo, cream cheese, lemon juice, dill weed, black pepper, and dijon mustard and mix well.
Chop off the stem and peel off 2 of the outer layers of your iceberg lettuce.
Layer the 2 layers of lettuce on top of each other and add in your tuna mix, diced cucumbers, and avocado slices inside the lettuce.
Roll it like a burrito and wrap it with sandwich paper and enjoy!

Pro tip: Make the tuna mix in advance and the day your want to eat it, assemble your wrap (takes less than 5 minutes). This preserves that crunch and prevents the wrap from getting soggy versus storing it overnight!

name: Lazy Chicken Udon
blurb: I call it "lazy" because of how quick and simple it is to make. You just throw in a few ingredients, mix in some seasoning and sauces, and make such a delicious, comforting meal. This is the type of meal that just warms you up and keeps you really full!
ingredients: 8oz raw chicken thigh, boneless skinless raw
steps: Dice your chicken thighs into small pieces, chop your napa cabbage, and dice your green onion into small pieces.
In a pot coated with spray oil on medium heat, sauté your cut chicken thighs & minced garlic.
Add in your napa cabbage, chicken broth, and water and let it boil.
Add in your soy sauce, miso paste, sliced cabbage, mushrooms, salt, pepper, green onions, onion powder, and sesame oil.
In another pot of boiling water, boil your udon noodles and transfer the cooked noodles into cold water.
Add your cooked udon noodles into the pot of soup and enjoy!

name: Spring Roll Bowl
blurb: I know I said how much I love fresh spring rolls already, but this bowl variation has similar flavors but is presented in a completely different way. Even though I love fresh spring rolls, I get sick of them pretty fast. So this noodle bowl variation is something I love to make instead to switch things up!
steps: Start by boiling water in a pot and adding in your vermicelli noodles. Once the noodles are cooked, place the noodles into cold water.
In the same pot of water, boil your shrimp until it turns pink & curls. Remove, pat dry, and season with black pepper.
Dice your Persian cucumbers in to thin strips and chop your lettuce.
To make the sauce, add in your fish sauce, white wine, juice of a lime, pineapple juice, diced jalapeno, and minced garlic into a cup and stir.
Add your noodles, shrimp, sliced cucumbers, and diced lettuce.
Top it off with edamame and beansprouts and pour in your sauce and enjoy!

name: Korean-Inspired Egg Bites
blurb: If you're a fan of the egg bites you see at Starbucks, you'll love these. It's a Korean take on egg bites and in my opinion, elevates it to a whole nother level. And don't even get me started on that crazy cheese pull you get when you split it open... (macros without the mozzarella cheese)
ingredients: Optional: mozzarella cheese (not included in the macros/calories)
steps: Use a food processor to mince your jalapeno, carrots, onion, and kimchi.
Dump your mix into a bowl and add crack your eggs and add rice, drained light canned tuna, cornstarch, salt, and pepper and mix well.
Place the mix into your circular mold pan coated with spray oil on medium heat and cook until the edges start to crisp.
Once ready, carefully use a small spatula to flip them inside the mold to cook the other sides until golden brown.
This step is optional and will add extra calories, but I like to enjoy this best with a little mozzarella cheese between two patties. Enjoy!

name: Kimchi Jeon
blurb: This is a classic Korean recipe that my mom made me growing up. It's considered a savory, salty, and spicy dish but not many people realize just how nutrient dense it is with all that protein. If you want to impress your Korean crush or friends, this is the recipe to make them!
ingredients: 9oz light canned tuna in water (Chicken of the Sea Brand)
steps: Dice your green onions, jalapeño, and kimchi into small pieces and add them into a large bowl.
Add in your gochugaru, salt, flour, and water and mix well.
Drain your canned tuna and add it into the bowl and mix well until you have a batter- like consistency.
Spray cooking oil on a non-stick pan on medium heat and pour your batter in the center. Spread the batter thin and into a large circle the size of the pan without creating any holes or gaps.
Flip once the edges crisp and it slides freely on the pan when you shake it.
Top it off with leftover green onions and enjoy!

name: Dakgalbi
blurb: Dakgalbi or Stir Fried Spicy Korean chicken is a dish we often overlook as healthy, filling, and nutritious. The rice cakes and veggies make this a very satiating meal while the chicken thighs pack each serving with a ton of protein. It's also very similar taste wise to the iconic Korean dish Tteokbokki!
steps: Chop your napa cabbage, dice your green onions, slice your red onions, and cut your chicken into small pieces.
In a small bowl, add brown sugar, gochugaru, black pepper, soy sauce, sesame oil, gochujang, mirin, a curry cube, and minced garlic and your chicken pieces and mix well.
In a pan coated with spray oil on medium-low heat, sauté your marinated chicken until cooked through.
Add in your red onions, napa cabbage, green onions, and refrigerated rice cakes and sauté until everything is evenly marinated.
Top it off with sesame seeds and enjoy!

name: Rice Paper Scallion Pancake
blurb: Scallion pancakes are an iconic Chinese dish and there's nothing that quite compares to that super crispy, flaky texture, and savory taste. But they're not the most diet-friendly recipe with how much oil and dough is used in the process. So using rice paper is a great way to get that same chew and crunch while saving on hundreds of extra calories.
ingredients: pinch of salt and white pepper
steps: Mince your garlic and dice your green onions into small pieces.
Thaw, pat dry, then dice your frozen shrimp.
In a bowl, combine your diced shrimp, green onions, garlic, sesame oil, cornstarch, salt, and white pepper and mix well.

Wet your rice paper in water and place 1 of 5 equal portions of your shrimp mix on top in a line (do not over wet your rice paper as this will make them soggy and prone to breaking and sticking when grilling later).
Roll the rice paper into a thin log then fold the sides to seal the log shut.
Fold it into a spiral shape.
On a non-stick pan coated with spray oil on medium low heat, place your scallion pancakes and let them cook until golden brown and crispy on each side.
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, chili oil, sesame oil, and sesame seeds and mix. Dip you scallion pancakes in this sauce and enjoy!

name: Napa Cabbage Shrimp Dumpling Rolls
blurb: This recipe is one of my most viral recipes on my social media. If I have to guess why, I think it's because of how macro friendly they are. But the reason I love this recipe is just how filling it is. You get 6 rolls for 375 calories, which is insane because it's actually a ton of food which keeps me full for hours.
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Add your napa cabbage leaves into the boiling water until they start to become bendy and soft, but not to the point where they get super soft and soggy.
Immediately transfer them to a bowl of cold water.
Dice your green onions, cut you carrots into small pieces, and chop your shrimp onto small pieces.
In a bowl, add in your green onions, carrots, and shrimp and mix in minced garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, and black pepper and mix.
Lay your soft napa cabbage leaves flat and add your shrimp veggie mix onto the leaves.
Roll them into small dumplings with the shrimp mix filling inside.
In a pan on medium low heat coated with spray oil, add your "dumplings" and let them develop a brown sear on both sides and until the shrimp is cooked through.
Once ready, transfer the dumplings to your plate, pour your ponzu on top, and enjoy!

name: Gyeranjjim (Korean Steamed Egg)
blurb: Only 4 ingredients...but you get this incredibly fluffy, comforting dish that's perfect when paired with rice and some kimchi. Korean steamed egg is a dish I always order whenever I eat at KBBQ or at a korean restaurant, so making it at home lets me enjoy it more often. I like to make a few tweaks like using chicken bone broth to really bump up the protein content even further!
steps: In a Korean stone pot or a thick small pot, crack and whisk together your eggs.
Dice your green onions and add it in.
Pour in your chicken bone broth.
Add your salt and feel free to add more once cooked to adjust to your taste.
Mix everything well and cover with a lid to let it steam Cook over medium heat and once you start to see steam escape the lid, you know it's ready!
Optional: serve with rice and kimchi (not included in the macros)

name: Egg Drop Soup
blurb: This is another one of my most viewed recipes and is hands down the prettiest soup dish in this cookbook. There's just something about the fluffy egg ribbons that make this dish so pretty but also so delicious. Soups without a ton of chicken or beef aren't normally the most protein-rich, but this egg drop soup recipe is the one outlier.
ingredients: 1/8 tsp white pepper or more to taste
steps: In a bowl, crack and whisk 4 eggs and add in 1 tablespoon of water.
In a pot on medium heat, mix together chicken bone broth, chicken bouillon, garlic powder, salt, and diced green onions.
Create a cornstarch slurry in a new small bowl by mixing together 2 tbsp cornstarch and 3 tbsp water and slowly pour it into the pot as you continue to mix the broth.
Slowly pour your egg mixture into the pot as you mix the broth in a circular motion.
The thinner the pour, the smaller the egg ribbons.

name: Kimchi Tuna Melt
blurb: The concept behind this recipe is pretty simple. I love kimchi. I love tuna melts. So why not combine them together? And out of this experiment came a savory, salty, and cheesy sandwich that puts a tasty spin on the traditional tuna melt recipe we all love.
steps: Drain your canned tuna and add it into a bowl with your kimchi, gochujang, sesame oil, light mayo, and garlic powder.
Dice your green onions and add it into your bowl and mix it all together.
Get 2 slices of sourdough bread and sprinkle both your mozzarella and parmesan cheese on top of one slice of bread.

In a pan on medium-low heat coated with spray oil, toast both slices of bread in order to get a golden brown crisp on one side. Cover the pan with a lid to let the cheese cook through until it melts. Remove the slice with the melted cheese and only flip the slice of bread with no cheese and toast in the pan until golden brown again.
Place your tuna mix on top of the toast with cheese and then your slice of toasted sourdough on top to complete the sandwich.

name: Beef Enoki Rolls
blurb: The concept is pretty simple: we wrap our enoki mushrooms in thinly sliced beef and boil it in a umami rich broth topped with eggs. There's just so much flavor packed into these mushrooms beef rolls that soak up the broth that make this dish something I'd make for not only myself but also for my family to enjoy.
ingredients: 5oz thinly sliced beef brisket (found at your local Korean market)
Split your enoki mushrooms into small bundles.
Wrap yoor enoki mushroom bundles with your thinly sliced beef brisket like little
Place your beef enoki rolls in a pan and pour your soy sauce, water, and beef bone
broth and season with salt and pepper.
Cook it on medium heat and once the meat is cooked through, pour two beaten
eggs on top and top it off with diced green onions. Once the egg mixture cooks,
steps: Split your enoki mushrooms into small bundles.
Wrap yoor enoki mushroom bundles with your thinly sliced beef brisket like little burritos.
Place your beef enoki rolls in a pan and pour your soy sauce, water, and beef bone broth and season with salt and pepper.
Cook it on medium heat and once the meat is cooked through, pour two beaten eggs on top and top it off with diced green onions. Once the egg mixture cooks, you're ready to enjoy!

name: Mayak Eggs (Korean Marinated Eggs)
blurb: The word "mayak" in Korean literally translates to "drug" becasue of how addictingly good these eggs are. It's a great way to add a ton of flavor and protein to any dish. But unfortunately, they probably won't last very long in your fridge because they are just that good. I warned you!
steps: Dice your green onions, red peppers, and green peppers into small pieces.
Boil your eggs in a pot of boiling water for 6 minutes and immediately remove them from the boiling water and add them into cold water to create jammy eggs.
Peel your eggs under the cold water to make the peeling process easier.
In a bowl, combine your soy sauce, water, honey, mirin, minced garlic, sesame oil, diced green onions, diced red peppers, diced green peppers, and sesame seeds and mix well.
In a container, add your peeled eggs, pour your sauce, let it marinate for a few hours and enjoy!

name: Eomuk Bokkeum (Korean Stir Fried Fish Cake Side Dish)
blurb: This iconic Korean side dish is something you've likely seen at your local KBBQ or Korean restaurant. It's fish cake stir fried in a savory sauce that pairs as the perfect addition to any meal. I like making a whole batch of this and leaving it in my fridge to eat later in the week with any bland meal to really bump up the flavor!
ingredients: 200g sheet of fried fish cake (found at your local korean market)
steps: Thinly slice your onions and dice your green onion into small pieces.
Cut your fish cake into small strips.
In a bowl, mix together your brown sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and salt to taste.
In a pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, add your onions and fish cake then your green onions and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Add in your sauce and sauté for a few more minutes.
Top it off with sesame seeds then store it in an airtight container to enjoy later in the week!

name: Ojingeochae Muchim (Korean Spicy Dried Squid)
blurb: Korean spicy dried squid is something that brings me right back to my childhood. This is one of the few Korean side dishes you can enjoy with a meal and may still want to eat on it's own since it's just that good. And the best part is you don't have to do ANY cooking.
ingredients: 1 pack of Korean dried squid (40g) (found at your local korean market)
3 tbsp rice syrup (Ottogi Korean 100% Rice Syrup brand)
steps: In a bowl, add your gochujang paste, soy sauce, gochugaru, sesame oil, rice syrup, minced garlic and mix it together to make your sauce. Then add in your dried squid and mix well.
Place into an airtight container and enjoy later in the week with any meal!

name: Myeolchi Bokkeum (Korean Stir Fried Anchovies)
blurb: I know I know...anchovies. I used to have the exact same reaction as a kid whenever my mom would make these for the family. But the day I decided to try it, my perception of anchovies changed forever. These are nutty, savory, and addicting to just eat on it's own since it's packed with a ton flavor. Not to mention, this side dish packs a ton of protein per serving!
ingredients: 2 cups mini dried anchovies (found at your local korean market)
steps: In a pan coated with spray oil on medium heat, stir fry your peanuts for 1-2 minutes.
In a bowl, mix together your soy sauce, sesame oil, brown sugar, honey, and minced garlic to create your sauce.
Push the peanuts to the side and in the same pan, add in your dried mini anchovies and sauté until both the peanuts and anchovies become crunchy and light brown in color.
Turn off the heat (pan should still be hot), push the peanuts and anchovies to the side, and pour in your sauce.
In the pan, push your anchovies and peanuts into the sauce and mix well.
Let it cool down and place in an air tight container to enjoy now or for up to 3-4 weeks in the refrigerator!

name: Jangjorim (Korean Marinated Braised Beef)
blurb: This Korean marinated braised beef recipe is the perfect pairing to some rice and some kimchi. It's not only super tender but it's marinade is easily one of the most flavorful things you'll try. One of my best friends works at a tradition Korean restaurant and after trying my Jangjorim recipe, said it's the best he's ever had so I hope that says something.
steps: Peel your garlic cloves and dice your jalapeños into small pieces and thinly slice your onion.
Cut your raw meat into small cubes.
In a pot of boiling water, cook your meat for 7 minutes. Then, drain the water and impurities.
In a new pot filled with water, cook your meat on medium heat for 45 minutes. Then, drain the water once again.
In a new pot with just the meat, add 1/2 cup water, fresh garlic cloves, diced onion, soy sauce, and jalapeño slices and stir well while cooking for 15 minutes on medium heat.
Let it cool down, tear apart the beef with your fingers into small strips, and pour it all into an air tight container to enjoy later!

name: Gyeran-Mari (Korean Rolled Omelette)
blurb: Whenever I go to any breakfast diner, my friends always know I order omelettes. Nothing beats them as a healthy, nutritious, and protein-packed way to start your day. But eating them at home every day can get a little repetitive. So I find myself enjoying these Korean rolled omelettes really often. There's honestly nothing quite like how fluffy and soft these omelettes are, and I like to pair it with some kimchi and rice for a full meal.
ingredients: 1 tbsp green or red bell pepper
steps: Crack your eggs in a bowl.
Dice your white onion, bell pepper, and carrot into small pieces and add it into the bowl.
Add salt and pepper into the bowl and whisk well.
On a pan coated with spray oil on low heat, pour a very thin layer of your egg mixture and spread it around in the pan to create a circular, thin layer of egg.
Once the egg is cooking and almost fully set at the top, fold the egg over into itself like a burrito.

Keep folding it over on top of itself while pulling it back to allow yourself to have space on the pan to add more of your egg mixture on the pan that connects to the previous cooked portion, and continue the process until you have one large "egg burrito." Cut the "egg burrito" and enjoy. It's best served with rice and kimchi, which is not accounted for in the macros/calories.

name: Sangchu Geotjeori (Spicy Korean Salad)
blurb: This Spicy Korean Salad is something you've likely seen at your local KBBQ spot. It's that salad they serve with all of the side dishes thats spicy, savory, and super addicting to eat. In all honestly, it's my faovrite part of KBBQ and I can't properly enjoy KBBQ without it. In my version, I use slightly reduced ratios of oil and sauces to get the same flavors while reducing hundreds of extra calories. This is easily my most re-made recipe in my cookbook since it's so easy to create and makes eating my greens something I actually look forward to.
steps: Chop your lettuce into small pieces and cut your green onions into long thin strips.
In a bowl, combine your minced garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, gochugaru, sesame oil, sesame seeds and chopped veggies and mix well and enjoy!

name: Japchae (Sweet Potato Noodle Stir Fry)
blurb: Everyone loves this iconic Korean side dish. But if you've never tried it, I promise you need to once in your lifetime or you're missing out on one of the most delicious and umami-packed noodle dishes out there. But it normally is packed with a ton of calories so I like making it with sirloin beef, less oil, and more veggies to make it more filling and nutrient-dense.
ingredients: black pepper and salt to taste
4 oz of uncooked dangmyeon (Korean sweet potato starch or glass noodles)
steps: Dice your mushroom, carrots, and red bell pepper into small pieces, thinly slice your yellow onion, and slice your beef into small pieces.
Boil a pot of water, add in your spinach for 2 minutes, then immediately blanch it in ice cold water.
In a pan on medium heat coated with spray oil, sauté your cut mushrooms, yellow onion, bell pepper, carrots, and beef.
Immediately add in minced garlic, brown sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and black pepper and salt to taste, and mix until beef is cooked through.
Boil a pot of water, add in your glass noodles, then immediately transfer the cooked noodles into cold water to cool it down.
Turn the pan to low heat and add the cooked glass noodles, boiled spinach, and sesame seeds into the pan and mix well and enjoy!

name: Oi-Muchim (Korean Spicy Cucumber)
blurb: Korean Spicy cucumber is the best way to enjoy cucumbers. There I said it. This might be a controversial take, but I just love the fresh crunch this Korean side dish adds while giving a slightly sweet but spicy and savory punch of flavor in every bite.
steps: Slice your cucumbers into small circles, add it into a bowl, add in your salt, and mix well. Set aside for 10 minutes to let it drain the water from the cucumber.
Rinse the cucumbers and drain the liquid. Pat the cucumbers dry over a paper towel.
Combine thinly sliced white onions, gochugaru, rice vinegar, brown sugar, minced garlic, sesame oil, gochujang, toasted sesame seeds, and sliced cucumbers in a bowl.
Mix well and enjoy!

name: Sigeumchi-Namul (Korean Marinated Spinach)
blurb: If you struggle to enjoy your greens, I'm confident I can change your opinion after you try this dish. Spinach is not my favorite vegetable out there, but when made with these Korean flavors, it turns into a delicious side dish. This recipe is one of the few that make me actually want to reach for more veggies.
steps: In a pot of boiling water, add in your spinach for 1-2 minutes than quickly transfer it to a bowl of cold water to blanch it.
Remove the spinach from the cold water and form it into a ball to squeeze out any excess water.
Chop the ball of spinach into 4 equal pieces.
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, diced green onions, and sesame seeds and then add in your cut spinach and mix well.
Transfer to an airtight container and sore in your refrigerator to enjoy later!

name: Spicy Soondubu (Korean Spicy Tofu Soup)
blurb: In my top 5 favorite soups of all time, Soondubu HAS to be there. It's the most frequent order I get when I eat out at a Korean restaurant and is THE definition of Korean comfort food. For my recipe, I like using beef bone broth and an egg to bump up the protein content of the dish even more.
ingredients: 1 tbsp jalapeno pepper (add more or less to desired spice level)
steps: Thinly slice your red onions, green onions, and jalapeño.
In a pot coated with spray oil on medium heat, add in your diced veggies and sauté them.
Add in soy sauce, oyster sauce, beef bone broth, gochugaru, beef bone broth, dashi powder, minced garlic, and sesame oil and bring it to a boil.
Add chunks of silken tofu and crack in an egg and cover the lid to let the egg poach.
Once the tofu is soft and the egg is poached, salt to taste and enjoy!
Optional: This recipe pairs best with a cup of steamed rice (which is not included in the macros/calories)

name: Miyeokguk (Korean Seaweed Beef Soup)
blurb: In Korean culture, Miyeokguk is traditionally eaten on your birthday. But, I like making it whenever because it's also a tasty and nutrient-dense meal. The seaweed during the soaking and cooking process becomes super soft and silky, turning into the most tasty part of the meal.
ingredients: 1/3 cup dried seaweed aka cut, dried Wakame or Miyeok (not be confused with
steps: Slice your beef into small cubes.
In a large bowl of water and beef bone broth, add in your cut dried seaweed.
Let it soak for 15-20 minutes.
In a pot on medium heat, add your sesame oil, soy sauce, and cut beef and sauté until cooked through.
Squeeze the liquid out of your seaweed and add it into the pot, sautéing it all for a 2- 3 minutes.
Pour in the leftover beef bone broth & water mixture that your seaweed was originally soaking in back into the pot with some minced garlic and salt to taste and enjoy!

name: Kimchi Jjigae (Korean Spicy Kimchi Beef Stew)
blurb: This is a classic. If you like spice, kimchi, or stews, this is a recipe you'll want to make sure to try. I know I've perfected this recipe by now since even my Korean mom, who grew up in the heart of Seoul, thinks my recipe is the best Kimchi Jjigae she's ever had.
ingredients: 4 oz thinly sliced beef brisket, raw (found at your local Korean market)
steps: Slice your tofu into rectangles, thinly slice your yellow onion, and dice your mushrooms and green onions into small pieces.
In a pot on medium-high heat coated with spray oil, sauté the yellow onion and minced garlic. Add in your beef, cut kimchi, sliced mushrooms and continue to sauté for 1 minute.
Add in your beef bone broth, kimchi juice, brown sugar, gochugaru, gochujang, and soy sauce and bring it to a boil for a few minutes.
Add in your sliced tofu topped with green onions and season with salt or add in extra kimchi juice to taste and enjoy!

name: Ddukguk (Korean Beef Rice Cake Soup)
blurb: If you need to impress a Korean, this is the way to do it. Every Korean loves this soup since it's something your family always eats during the New Years as a part of Korean tradition. But I especially like making this soup on days where it's cold when I just need a warm, comforting meal.
ingredients: 2 tbsp cut pieces of roasted seaweed
steps: Cut your meat into small cubes.
In a pot coated with avocado oil on medium heat, cook your meat.
Add in your beef bone broth, water, minced garlic, and soy sauce and bring it to a boil.
Add in your refrigerated korean rice cakes and sesame oil and season to taste with salt and black pepper and let it continue to cook for a few minutes until the rice cakes and meat are cooked.
In a bowl, crack and whisk your egg. In a pan coated with spray oil on medium-low heat, pour your egg thinly to create a super thin round omelette.
Once the egg is cooked, place it on a cutting board, roll it into a burrito, and dice it to create little egg ribbons/slices.
In a bowl, pour your soup and top it off with diced green onions, half of your egg ribbons, and half of your shredded toasted seaweed and enjoy!

name: Muguk (Korean Beef & Radish Soup)
blurb: Korean beef & radish soup is a simple classic. It takes a bit of time to make. But when done, it's well worth the wait. If you're looking for a clear, clean broth that will just warm you up, this is the one. It's also packed with collagen, packed with protein, and most importantly, very filling.
ingredients: 1/2 pound thick beef brisket (commonly found at your local Korean market)
Optional: best enjoyed with 1 cup steamed rice (not included in the macros/calories)
steps: Peel your Korean radish.
Dice your Korean radish into small cubes.
In a large pot, add your water and radish slices and bring it to a boil.
Add into the boiling water your beef brisket cut into small cubes, minced garlic, chopped green onions, fish sauce, and salt and black pepper to taste.
Boil until the radish is soft and the meat is cooked through and enjoy!
